results.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Flow-Based Generalist Robot Policies
results.text:
2026 · Ralf Römer, Maximilian Seeliger, Liu S · 1 citations · Journal Article
TL;DR: This paper presents VFD, a method to quantify epistemic uncertainty in flow-matching models, and SAVE, a method for uncertainty-guided active multitask fine-tuning, to enhance failure awareness and adaptation of generalist robot policies in non-stationary environments.
Abstract: Generalist robot policies, such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs), combine powerful pretrained backbones with expressive generative action heads trained via flow matching on large-scale robotic datasets. Despite their strong empirical performance in robotic manipulation, these policies lack mechanisms to quantify confidence in their predictions and to detect when their actions may be unreliable. This presents a critical limitation for real-world deployment in non-stationary environments, where models inevitably encounter scenarios outside their pretraining…

results.title: The Geometry of Flow-Matching Uncertainty: A Cost-free Uncertainty Proxy and Its Application in Flow-based VLA Failure Detection
results.text:
2026 · Ziyang Rao, Yiren Zhao, Weiyu Guo · Journal Article
TL;DR: Researchers introduce denoising acceleration (accel), a cost-free uncertainty proxy for flow-matching models, measuring deviation from an ideal contraction field, and demonstrate its effectiveness in online failure detection, outperforming costly baselines in realistic deployment settings.
Abstract: Flow matching (FM) has become a popular action head paradigm for modern embodied models. However, as a conditional generative model, it does not explicitly expose its inherent uncertainty, producing faulty action chunks even when it misinterprets the scene or encounters out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. Therefore, determining when an FM-generated action can be trusted is essential for safe deployment, yet existing uncertainty estimation methods on real-time control suffer from several issues: extra training budget, high computational overhead, and low generalization ability. results.text:
2026 · Sai Navaneet Peddapalli, Sangmoon Lee, Sangtae Ahn · Journal Article
TL;DR: This paper proposes SUas mentioned in this paperlow, a state-space uncertainty-aware residual flow matching framework for robust robot manipulation, achieving 92.5% average success rate on LIBERO and comparable performance to large VLAs on LIBERO-PRO with significantly fewer parameters.
Abstract: Generative vision-language-action policies have advanced robot manipulation, but they often exhibit instability under noise, partial observability, and stochastic initial conditions. During extended rollouts, small velocity errors accumulate, degrading execution reliability. Existing diffusion and flow-based policies typically assume homoscedastic residuals and lack explicit uncertainty modeling within action generation, limiting robustness during iterative rollout. We propose SUREFlow, a state-space uncertainty-aware residual flow matching framework built on a Mamba backbone. The method…

results.title: Perturbation-Based Epistemic Uncertainty for Failure Detection in Vision-Language-Action Models
results.text:
2026 · YouSung Lee, Dongsoo Har · Journal Article
TL;DR: We propose perturbation-based failure detection (PFD) for Vision-Language-Action models, estimating epistemic uncertainty through low-rank weight perturbations, achieving the highest AUROC and balanced accuracy among evaluated methods, and outperforming stochastic action sampling under distribution shifts.
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong performance in robotic manipulation, but reliable uncertainty quantification remains challenging, particularly under distribution shift. Unlike autoregressive policies, many modern VLA models generate continuous actions through regression or flow-based generation, where explicit predictive probabilities are unavailable. Moreover, stochastic action sampling primarily captures action-generation variability under a fixed model, while failure detection under distribution shift can benefit from capturing uncertainty in the model itself.…

results.title: What to Reuse in Generative Robot Policies? A Solver-Aware Mathematical Analysis of Training-Free Output Caching for Action Generation
results.text:
2026 · Jiwon Kim, Jaekwon Lee, Jaekwon Lee · Mathematics · Journal Article
TL;DR: Researchers analyze training-free output caching for generative robot policies, revealing numerical degeneracy in explicit Euler integrators and amplification of staleness error in stochastic ancestral samplers, leading to a stable endpoint-space caching protocol, EndCache, with 2.7× speedup and 85.9% task success.
Abstract: Diffusion- and flow-matching-based generative robot policies, including recent vision–language–action (VLA) models, generate continuous action chunks by repeatedly invoking an action generator over multiple generation steps, which constitutes a major bottleneck for real-time robot control. Training-free output caching—recomputing the generator only at selected steps and reusing its output in between—is an attractive remedy, but its mathematical properties and stability criteria have not been rigorously examined for robot action generation. This paper provides a solver-aware mathematical…

results.title: Potential-Guided Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Policy Improvement
results.text:
2026 · Yunpeng Mei, Jiakai He, Hongjie Cao · 1 citations · Journal Article
TL;DR: This paper introduces ForesightFlow, a self-guided flow-matching policy that improves vision-language-action policy performance by augmenting generated action chunks with learned success-potential trajectories, and decouples advantage-weighted flow matching to prevent value hallucination.
Abstract: Large vision-language-action (VLA) policies are increasingly trained as conditional generative models over action chunks. Yet deployment produces mixed-quality experience-successful demonstrations, partial completions, recoverable mistakes, and failures-that is difficult to use with standard imitation. Full behavior cloning (BC) imitates failures, filtered BC discards useful sub-trajectories, and offline reinforcement learning adds a large critic. We introduce ForesightFlow, a self-guided flow-matching policy that augments each generated action chunk with a learned success-potential…

results.title: Fewer Steps, Better Actions: Rethinking Flow-Matching Inference for VLA Policies
results.text:
2026 · Zhipeng Tang, Xinda Chen, Weining Rao · Journal Article
TL;DR: Researchers propose Coda, a method that reallocates integration steps to a learned endpoint correction, improving VLA policy success (71.64% to 74.68%) while reducing latency (30.2%) and increasing speed (2.12x) on RoboTwin Easy tasks.
Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies based on flow matching generate action chunks through repeated evaluations of an action expert. Increasing the number of integration steps raises inference cost, but does not necessarily improve closed-loop success. We propose Coda, which reallocates part of this integration budget to a single learned endpoint correction. A frozen policy first completes a few-step noise-to-action trajectory; a lightweight Transformer then predicts a demonstration-supervised residual using the candidate action, source noise, and shared observation-prefix cache. results.title: When Can Conditional Flow Matching Replace Pointwise Negative Log-Likelihood?
results.text:
2026 · Yansen Han, Hongxin Sun, Tao Lin · Journal Article
TL;DR: Conditional flow matching (CFM) can replace pointwise negative log-likelihood (NLL) under specific conditions, including linear Gaussian paths and the use of a weighted CFM objective, but this is not generally true for training or on-policy alignment.
Abstract: Flow matching enables likelihood-free training, yet alignment methods increasingly reuse conditional flow matching (CFM) losses as endpoint negative log-likelihoods (NLLs) and their old/new differences as log-likelihood ratios. We characterize when these substitutions are valid. For linear Gaussian paths, we exactly decompose endpoint NLL into entropy, a weighted CFM objective, an interior velocity--score residual, and a boundary residual. Thus CFM-only estimates and differences are exact only when the corresponding residuals cancel. At the off-policy population optimum, ordinary CFM is not…

results.title: Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision for Reliable Dual-Arm Surgical Subtask Manipulation
results.text:
2026 · Mingwu Su, Guankun Wang, Jinsong Lin · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study proposes Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision (TDHD), a test-time mechanism that estimates action reliability by measuring trajectory divergence under small noise perturbations, improving performance of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in surgical robotic manipulation by 5-25% across needle and tissue manipulation tasks.
Abstract: Surgical robotic systems are increasingly being adopted as clinical workload rises, motivating autonomous solutions for repetitive manipulation subtasks. Learning-based controllers improve generalization compared with rule-based and analytic approaches, but most are trained for individual tasks and remain difficult to reuse across procedures. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models provide a unified framework that integrates visual perception, language grounding, and action generation, offering a promising path toward more composable surgical autonomy. results.title: Breaking Flow-Matching Embodied Policies with Trajectory-Coupled Adversarial Perturbations
results.text:
2026 · Mengxiang Liu, Ruilong Deng, Siyuan Pan · Security and safety · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study proposes the Tau-Path Coupled Attack (TPCA), a visual attack that leverages flow-rollout coupling to induce task failure in flow-matching VLA policies, outperforming endpoint-only optimization in action-space endpoint displacement and task failure rates on LIBERO spatial tasks.
Abstract: Flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies generate actions through $\tau$-indexed ordinary differential equation (ODE) rollouts, exposing intermediate velocity-field structure that endpoint-only adversarial objectives do not directly target. We study this mechanism on the evaluated $\pi_{0.5}$ policy in LIBERO and propose the Tau-Path Coupled Attack (TPCA), a white-box visual attack that couples executed-window endpoint displacement with velocity-field divergence along the flow rollout. The study is deliberately scoped as a single-architecture mechanism analysis rather than a…

results.title: WAM-Flow: Wasserstein Action Manifolds for Vision-Language-Action Policy Alignment and Optimal-Transport Flow-Matching Decoding
results.text:
2026 · Haopeng Jin · Journal Article
TL;DR: This paper introduces WAM-Flow, a geometric formulation of action decoding for vision-language-action policies, using Wasserstein Action Manifolds to align and match optimal-transport flow-matching decoding, addressing quantization and temporal structure mismatch in existing methods.
Abstract: WAM-Flow technical report / preprint. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies commonly decode actions either through discrete tokenization or through continuous Euclidean regression. Both choices can be mismatched to robot control semantics: tokenization introduces irreversible quantization, while Euclidean losses ignore task-dependent temporal, cross-joint, and embodiment structure [Brohan et al., 2023; Kalashnikov et al., 2023; Team et al., 2024; Black et al., 2024]. results.title: GeoAAC: Geometry-Based Adaptive Action Chunking from Denoising Trajectories in VLA Policies
results.text:
2026 · Xin Chen, Sen Chen, Yujuan Ding · Journal Article
TL;DR: GeoAAC, a geometry-based adaptive action chunking method, adjusts the action horizon in VLA policies based on the reliability of action predictions, leveraging the geometry of denoising trajectories to improve performance by up to 8.7% in simulation and 21.1% in real-world tasks.
Abstract: Action chunking is widely used for action generation and execution in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, yet existing approaches commonly use a fixed action horizon. During a rollout, different task stages may require different levels of action continuity, control precision, and closed-loop feedback, making a fixed horizon unable to accommodate changing control requirements. We propose \textbf{GeoAAC}, a geometry-based adaptive action chunking method for flow-based VLA policies that adjusts the action horizon according to the reliability of the current action prediction.
